A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, The Complexity of Correlated Equilibria in Generalized Games. All pages, including Appendices A–C, are readable; the equations and illustrative figure support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents complexity reductions, mathematical proofs, and illustrative constructions, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The added autobidding discussion reports no original empirical results.

M1.justification: The reduction strategies remain the same, but the membership construction changes: Section 4 removes the identity blocks and corresponding zero entries from A and b, and Claim 4.5 revises the internal approximation parameters. These are localized changes to the computational reduction.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or experimental tasks. The expanded discussion of Internet advertising introduces application context, not an evaluated domain.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. References to equilibrium algorithms and additional cited work are theoretical context, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to approximation parameters concern mathematical reductions, not evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. Figure 1 and Appendix A retain their illustrative theoretical examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries, performance rankings, or measured numerical outcomes in either version. Revised theoretical guarantees and bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Sections 2.2–3 change admissible deviations from cost at most ν to cost at most zero, while allowing the equilibrium distribution itself cost at most ν. Lemma 3.3 and Equation (2) consequently require deviating marginals to match exactly. Section 4 and Appendix C revise the constraint correspondence, and Claim 4.5 receives new tolerance choices and a substantially rewritten proof of safety, deviation simulation, and equilibrium conditions. These changes alter the formal problem and its membership argument.

C1.justification: The PPAD-completeness headline is retained, but the computational problem referenced by the main contribution now requires stability only against exactly safe deviations, rather than all ν-safe deviations. This substantively redefines the central guarantee. Section 1.1 also adds an explicit impossibility claim for general efficient no-regret convergence and its application to black-box autobidding.

C2.justification: The added discussion in Section 1.1 explains why equilibrium convergence matters for advertising platforms and argues that convergence guarantees must exploit application-specific structure. The existing interpretation of correlation versus coupled constraints and the open question about constant approximations remain.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies software implementation settings, hardware information, experimental processing instructions, or code/data access information. The added construction and normalization details concern mathematical proofs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hart and Mas-Colell (2000), Agarwal et al. (2014), Balseiro et al. (2021), and Paes Leme et al. (2024) to support the learning and autobidding discussion. It also adds Ni et al. (2025) to the discussion of equilibrium existence without strict feasibility. The central positioning against earlier complexity results remains.

P1.justification: v2 adds a focused introductory discussion, reorganizes Claim 4.5's proof into three named steps, adds a normalization footnote and acknowledgment, and makes small wording and cross-reference edits. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and its caption are unchanged, but its placement relative to the surrounding argument shifts. The Appendix C.1 matrix display becomes shorter after block removal, and the expanded proof changes equation placement and page layout. There are no new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central membership argument. It removes v1's identity-block constraints, which imposed nonpositive coordinates alongside a unit-sum requirement, and replaces the unsupported deviation-simulation step with an explicit derivation and revised error bounds in Appendix C.2. The material tradeoff is that this argument establishes the revised, weaker incentive condition against exactly safe deviations, rather than v1's claimed guarantee against all ν-safe deviations.
